source_text: This resilience stemmed primarily from internal religious imperatives rather than external legal pressures, with successive Dai al-Mutlaq endorsing the ritual—Daim al-Islam citing benefits like hygiene and urge control post-age seven—outweighing nascent secular influences until diaspora activism intensified scrutiny in the 2010s.
